clue.text: Struggle as gas blows back in face

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the word for struggle

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: blowing back sends the word gas the other way, so it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned

explanation.surface: A fight breaks out while a gust of gas blows back into someone's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows back' turns the gas round, and 'in' places it inside the struggle word; 'as' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Visage is a literary synonym for a person's face or countenance.

clue.text: Liveliness of exam on Paris, say

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination, especially at university
Paris is an example of a city

explanation.surface: A student's spirited performance in an exam about the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first piece sits above the second; 'say' signals that Paris is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity is a noun meaning sparkle, animation or high spirits, a straight synonym of liveliness.

clue.text: Leave office and return to ground?

definitions.meaning: to resign from a post or position
literally to put a foot down again from a height, coming back to ground level

explanation.definitionFit: Stepping down is both resigning a post and literally descending a step to the floor.

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are taken, so the answer is buried in them

explanation.surface: Someone almost passed away a while back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a hidden word: it runs across 'aGO NEarly'. 'time' belongs to the surface only, as a link before the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone is a common euphemism for having died, as in 'he's gone now'.

parts.note: as can mean since or because
sorted means put in order or arranged

explanation.surface: A jumble that was once neatly arranged is now in a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means of various kinds mixed together, as in a box of mixed-up chocolates.

parts.note: read 'temporarily' as 'in terms of time': things that cannot be separated in time happen at the same moment

explanation.definitionFit: Events happening at exactly the same time cannot be separated in time, which is what the word describes.

indicators.note: taking something from a word means removing its letter

parts.note: a joust is a tournament contest between mounted knights
J is the abbreviation for jack on playing cards

explanation.surface: A knight is thrown out of a medieval tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' removes J (jack, as on playing cards) from JOUST, a knights' contest suggested by 'tourney'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to eject or expel them from a place or position.

clue.text: Part of shirt, or its maker?

parts.note: the tail is the long lower part of a shirt, tucked in

explanation.surface: A question of whether we mean a piece of a shirt or the person who made it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its maker' refers back to the shirt: the person who makes shirts and suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor is the craftsman who makes clothes such as shirts and suits.

definitions.meaning: the Baskerville family in the Sherlock Holmes story was haunted by a hound, so playfully they were hound-ridden

explanation.definitionFit: Dogged means tenaciously pursued, and humorously describes a family plagued by a dog.

clue.text: After bomb, girl returned to capital

indicators.note: the girl comes after the bomb in the answer

parts.note: the V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War, written VI

indicators.note: returned means the name is read back to front

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: After an air raid, a young woman made her way back to the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: The V1 was a German flying bomb of the Second World War. 'returned' reverses the girl's name, and 'After' puts it behind the bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria.

clue.text: Helping to prepare spuds on Sunday? Great!

indicators.note: one piece on another in an across clue follows it

parts.note: mashing is a way of preparing potatoes, spuds being potatoes

explanation.surface: Someone excitedly volunteers to mash the potatoes for Sunday lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: Spuds are potatoes in British slang. MASHING goes 'on' (after) S for Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Smashing is a British colloquial exclamation of approval meaning great or excellent.

clue.text: Establishment of business, with another in the country

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: in places the second business inside the country

parts.note: a nation is a country
another business is a firm

explanation.surface: Setting up a company that merges with a rival in some country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another business, which goes 'in' the country after its first letter, so the business abbreviation leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Confirmation is the establishing of something as true or valid, so the two words share that sense.

clue.text: Start to criticise poem it's unreadable

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a poem as impossible to read.
explanation.definitionFit: A code, until cracked, is writing that cannot be read by outsiders.

indicators.note: holding means the word for promise contains the money

parts.note: giving your word is promising
L is the abbreviation for pound, a unit of money

explanation.surface: Someone with cash in hand promises the earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' puts L (pound, from Latin libra) inside WORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The world is the earth, the planet we live on.

parts.note: C stands for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Asking for a chilly ice-cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is an ice-cream served in a conical wafer, so it names the treat.

definitions.meaning: a hooked staff, the crosier, carried by a bishop

explanation.definitionFit: A crook is both a criminal and the hooked pastoral staff a bishop holds.

parts.note: to bear is to carry
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Wearing diamonds woven into one's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A beard is the hair growing on a man's chin and cheeks, an example of hair.

parts.note: a tall building whose building, in the Bible, led to the confusion of languages; highly suggests its height

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the tall tower's building was stopped when God confused the builders' languages.

indicators.note: work as a verb means to shape or rework, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is instructed to go and look for extra jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges the letters of FIND MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informed means told or notified of something.

parts.note: re means about or concerning
par means level or equal, as in on a par
a tee is the golfer's peg the ball is placed on

explanation.surface: A golfer making jokes about being level on a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR and TEE are both golf terms, which suits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick witty conversation, so it is a synonym of wit.

clue.text: Found caterer prepared for sporting event

indicators.note: prepared means made ready or worked up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A food supplier has been lined up for a big sports day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges the twelve letters of FOUND CATERER.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous French cycle race held each summer is a major sporting event.

clue.text: Not formally promoted on the boards?

definitions.meaning: temporarily doing a senior job without the official rank
the boards are the stage, so performing in a play

explanation.definitionFit: Acting means doing a job temporarily, as an acting manager, and performing on stage.

clue.text: Part of suit, not VAT returnable

indicators.note: returnable means the pieces are sent back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a vat is a large tub

explanation.surface: A suit is offered without VAT and can be taken back to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT here is a tub, not the tax. 'returnable' reverses NOT plus TUB together.
explanation.definitionFit: A button is a fastening that forms part of a suit jacket.

clue.text: See the light when you crack this

definitions.text: See the light when you crack this

parts.words: See the light when you crack this
parts.note: solving one of these brings understanding, a flash of enlightenment

explanation.definitionFit: Cracking a crossword hint makes the solver suddenly understand, which describes the thing itself.

parts.note: an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: Someone in great shape who nevertheless cannot concentrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like an adjective for healthy, but here it is a noun, a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Vague means unclear or lacking sharp focus.

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

explanation.surface: Someone retrieved an old-fashioned outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The toga was the garment worn by citizens of ancient Rome.

indicators.note: full of means the word for friend contains the other letter

parts.note: a pal is a friend
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Phoning a lively friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a ringing of bells, so the noun ring fits.

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned, read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a jockey who is riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone says they are riding over to see a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses AM plus UP as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: The puma is a large wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: In cheeky comeback, I'd appear bold

indicators.note: a comeback turns the word around so it is read backwards

parts.note: pert means cheeky or saucy

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a cheeky retort will make them look brave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reverses the cheeky word to TREP, which sits between the two plain pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and daring, a synonym of bold.

clue.text: Fit to receive medal, attaining peak

indicators.note: the first word receives the medal inside it

parts.note: to suit is to fit or be right for
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: Someone worthy of a medal for reaching a mountaintop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Medal is a British gallantry award; 'to receive' puts its initials inside the word for fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the top of a mountain, its peak.

clue.text: Good at fishing, having long limbs

parts.note: angling is fishing with a rod and line

explanation.surface: Someone tall and lanky turns out to be a skilled angler.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone tall, thin and loose-jointed with long arms and legs.

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A labourer and the French reach an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle a problem is to deal with or manage it.
